title: URL and domain reputation gate before fetch and navigation, then layered screening (reviewer model, Quarry-side injection labels)
summary: Add a ReputationProvider trait in quarry-security that SecurityEngine.preflight and the agent validate_navigation hook call before any fetch, redirect or discovered crawl link. Start with a local hash-prefix list (Web Risk Update-style) so full URLs never leave the platform, add per-org modes (off, normal, customer secure-web-gateway categories such as Zscaler) in Control Plane, and never persist verdicts for ZDR orgs. || Three optional defence-in-depth layers. Model Plane: a fixed-rubric, tool-less reviewer model that can pre-approve low-risk first-visit approvals (never hand-off or always-confirm tiers), fails closed, caches allow per (thread, origin) with a short TTL and logs decisions in receipts. Ingestion Plane: a local, hashed-prefix reputation check in egress policy (decision_source=site_status) evaluated with the domain grant. Quarry scrape/extract: an opt-in prompt-injection flag that labels suspicious spans or fails with a typed error.
whyItMatters: Autonomous browsing can reach phishing or malware pages, and enterprise customers want their own secure-web-gateway policy applied to Verevon's agent traffic. validate_navigation already gates every Model-proposed navigation, so the hook exists and the feature is a strong enterprise-sales point. || Cuts approval fatigue and supports unattended scheduled runs, protects agents from phishing and injection farms, and gives direct Quarry API consumers the same guard the agent path already has.

others: Codex in-app browser (guardian v2 reviewer with {thread, origin} cache and 5-minute expiry, credential rubric and evidence fencing; site_status reputation endpoint with per-origin cache)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique || Reviewer 1 of 3 (unique); reputation 1 of 3 (unique); injection guard 3 of 3 (table-stakes, Verevon agent path already covered)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: checkUrl(url, orgConfig): local allow/deny lists and blocked TLDs, then optional customer SWG category rules synced on an interval, then a reputation provider (Google Web Risk hash-prefix database or a batched Zscaler lookup) with a risk threshold and an explicit fail-open or fail-closed policy. It runs before the first engine and on every redirect and discovered link. Modes are off, manual, normal, zscaler. Verdicts are cached only within the request, which respects the ZDR boundary, and a per-request override is allowed only if org config permits. || Merged items add: Approval request -> reviewer sub-agent with {action, origin, sanitized URL, bounded transcript}; returns allow|deny|escalate; missing evidence is never permission. Reputation: lookup(origin, path) in a cache, call the service on miss, deny blocked categories. Injection: neutralise role-tag lookalikes, wrap in BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED markers, optionally classify chunks with a small model.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: quarry-security has SSRF heuristics, URL-signature analysis and blocklists but no reputation provider and no customer SWG integration (no WebRisk or reputation code found). The right hook, validate_navigation, is already called for Model-proposed navigation and recovery actions. || Execution-core screens ExternalWeb/BrowserScraped/ThirdPartyMcp results unconditionally (shipped). No safety reviewer exists for browser approvals (capability-core's llmreviewer is a skill-learning reviewer), no reputation lookup was found in Quarry crates (only a capability flag cap.self_owned.quarry_url_reputation_feeds), and Quarry's observation path has no injection labelling for direct API consumers.

approachOriginal: Phase 1: reputation gate in SecurityEngine.preflight and validate_navigation (Google Web Risk or a customer-chosen provider, verdicts not stored, ZDR-safe). Phase 2 (from R-t2-09-13, lower priority): reviewer-model screening of approvals and Quarry-side trust labels on observations as part of the prompt-injection program. || Source detail: [R-t2-04-08] Ingestion Plane: ReputationProvider trait in quarry-security, called from SecurityEngine.preflight, validate_navigation, redirect handling and crawl-link discovery. Implement a local hash-prefix provider first (periodic list sync, local match, full-URL lookup only if a prefix matches and the org mode allows it), then an optional Zscaler adapter. Per-org mode and failure policy live in Control Plane and arrive through the policy floor (R-t2-04-05). Return ErrorCode::SecurityBlocked with a reputation sub-code and show a clear block message in the browser pane. No verdict persistence for ZDR orgs. || [R-t2-09-13] Model Plane: optional reviewer step in the approval pipeline for tiers marked pre-approvable. Ingestion Plane: local reputation feed in the egress policy; opt-in injection flag on scrape/extract while execution-core screening stays authoritative for agents. Build after per-origin consent (R-t2-09-08) and typed denials (R-t2-09-07).
risks: Lookup APIs that receive full URLs leak user intent (ZDR), hence the local-prefix design. False positives block legitimate research, so offer an allow-list and clear messages. || The reviewer can itself be prompt-injected (fence evidence, never sole gate for irreversible actions); cost per approval; do not send full ZDR URLs to third-party reputation services; classifier false positives.

verevon.exactGap: A feed-backed local host reputation list already exists: scripts/sync-security-feeds.py (operator-run, URLhaus CSV, optional PhishTank) writes a host blocklist snapshot that quarry-edge loads once at boot into DefaultEngine, and SecurityEngine.preflight (scrape path, pipeline.rs:305) plus validate_navigation (explicit Navigate actions and tab creation) consult it, so 'absent' is wrong. Missing are scheduled sync and hot reload (no runtime mutation path outside tests), subdomain or URL-level matching (exact host only), per-org modes (the quarry-control /v1/blocklists CRUD is not wired into the engine), enforcement on redirects, click-initiated navigations and subresources (quarry-browser's guard_navigation_target and guard_page_request_target use only the SSRF heuristic, not the engine; the DNS-pinned egress proxy with decision receipts is the natural seam), and any hash-prefix or customer-gateway provider. No safety-reviewer step or Quarry-side injection labelling exists, while Model Plane screening of external-trust results is already unconditional and cross-domain navigation is already a deterministic HITL approval category.

ZDR: no verdict persistence and no full URLs sent to third-party reputation services (hence local list or hash-prefix design). A Model Plane reviewer would put a model into the approval path although approvals are deterministic HITL today, and Quarry to Model Plane calls are not granted, so layers 2 and 3 need grants and an ADR and must never be the sole gate for irreversible tiers.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword phase 1 as 'automate and extend the existing feed-backed blocklist': scheduled sync job plus hot reload (swap the RwLock sets), suffix/subdomain matching, per-org mode via the policy floor, and a reputation callback in BrowserEgressPolicy / the egress proxy so redirects, click-driven navigations and subresources are covered and receipts carry a decision source (today validate_navigation covers only explicit Navigate actions). Introduce the ReputationProvider trait and a hash-prefix Web Risk style provider only if feed coverage proves insufficient; wire or retire the unconnected /v1/blocklists CRUD. Demote the reviewer-model screening, Quarry-side injection labels and any Zscaler or other customer-gateway adapter to optional follow-ups.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for phase 1 (extend existing engine, feed automation, egress hook, per-org mode); layers 2 and 3 are separate L-sized work behind grants.
verevon.verdictReason: The item claims no reputation provider exists but a URLhaus feed-backed host blocklist is already loaded by quarry-edge; the real gaps are automation, matching depth, per-org mode and redirect/click coverage at the egress boundary, and the reviewer layers should be demoted.

title: Fail-closed PII redaction stage for scraped and crawled content
summary: Add an optional redaction transform in the Ingestion Plane pipeline (after markdown, before LLM formats, diffing and Data Plane ingest) that calls the Model Plane language PII provider with entity types and a replace style (tag, mask, remove). Policy comes per org from the Control Plane; if redaction fails or exceeds a size limit the response returns empty content plus a warning.
whyItMatters: GDPR posture: orgs can ingest web content into the Data Plane without storing personal data, which complements ZDR. Today only model input is filtered, not what Quarry stores.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this record set (Firecrawl); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: After markdown derivation and before downstream transformers and LLM formats, send markdown plus {mode, entities, replaceStyle} to a redaction service with model, Presidio and spaCy accuracy tiers; replace spans; if the call fails or the size limit is exceeded, return empty markdown with a warning (fail closed).

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The Model Plane gateway redacts emails and long number sequences from model input under a pii_filter policy, and inference-core has a language provider with a Pii operation. Quarry scrape and crawl output and Data Plane ingest are not redacted. agent_memory::redact_sensitive is re-exported in lib.rs with no caller. Cost: the model-gateway grant to Quarry is still refused (see R-t2-02-02).

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane: add a redact stage in the transform pipeline gated by a per-org policy (Control Plane) and a per-request option on FormatSpec; call a Model Plane PII route (language provider) over the markdown; fail closed with a warning; run before json/summary formats and before hashing for change tracking so monitors do not store raw PII. Reuse the Model Plane deterministic pii_filter as a cheap first pass.
dependencies: model-gateway grant to quarry-edge (shared with F-t2-019)
planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (stage) with Model Plane (PII model) and Control Plane (policy)
risks: Over-redaction damages content and extraction quality; added latency on crawls; redaction accuracy claims need testing for Norwegian and other non-English text.

verevon.exactGap: SRC: nothing in the scrape/crawl path redacts content: PageRunner builds markdown, links and metadata (pipeline.rs:505-516) and persists the raw html artifact, the markdown artifact and meta.json (pipeline.rs:604-660) before the optional Data Plane ingest (pipeline.rs:855+), and quarry_runtime::redact_sensitive (agent_memory.rs:52) is used only by AgentScratchpad. SRC: the building blocks differ from the item's assumptions: Model Plane /v1/ai/language/pii accepts no entity-type or replace-style parameters (AiLanguageRequest, http_routes.rs:1947-1957; Azure parameters hard-code all categories and a '*' mask, language.rs:529), the deterministic pii_filter lives in model-gateway and is driven by capability-core safety_policies (moderation.rs:3-5,123), and quarry-edge holds no model-gateway audience (cross-plane-token-requests.json rows model-invoke, model-stream and model-audio are granted:false). DOC: SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md:97 and :218 already plan a redact_before_persist policy and a 'PII Redactor' pipeline stage, so this is planned but unbuilt rather than unplanned.
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/pipeline.rs:505-516 (markdown, links, metadata built; no redaction step)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/pipeline.rs:525 (fingerprint over raw body bytes) and :604-660 (html, markdown, meta.json artifacts persisted)

reuse: model-gateway moderation.rs redact_pii (deterministic first pass pattern)
quarry-core PrivacyPolicy::guard_third_party_processing to gate any PII provider as a third-party processor
Data Plane retrieval-engine-rs redact.rs regex set (email, phone, card) as a reference for a shared deterministic redactor
quarry-transform crate as the home for a pure, dependency-light redactor
Model Plane /v1/ai/language/pii as an optional second tier once a grant exists
verevon.constraints: SRC: org PII policy is owned by capability-core safety_policies in the Model Plane (moderation.rs:3-5), not the Control Plane, so 'policy comes per org from the Control Plane' misassigns ownership; no cross-plane DB access means Quarry must read it through an API or accept a per-request flag. SRC: sending page text to the Model Plane PII route is third-party processing (Azure AI Language) that needs the PrivacyPolicy processor gate and ZDR-eligible terms, and the model-gateway grant is currently refused (decision D16/QB-T17). SRC: redaction must cover every persisted representation, not just markdown: raw html artifact, markdown, meta.json, the local search index, page screenshots for visual RAG, and Data Plane ingest.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start with a deterministic in-process redactor in quarry-transform (regex plus checksum validators for emails, phone numbers, IBAN, card Luhn and the Norwegian 11-digit fodselsnummer mod-11) behind a per-request redact option and an org default read from the existing policy source; do not reuse redact_sensitive as-is because it whitespace-tokenizes and would flatten markdown. Make it fail closed at the persistence boundary (no html, markdown, meta, index or ingest write when redaction errors) instead of only blanking the response. Treat the Model Plane PII model as an optional second tier after the model-gateway grant lands, and extend its route with categories and replace style if needed.
verevon.effortNote: A deterministic stage over markdown alone is M; covering all persisted representations, the policy source and an optional model tier makes the item L.
verevon.verdictReason: Not shipped, but the item misstates policy ownership, ignores raw html and other persisted artifacts, assumes a Model Plane call that is not granted and parameters the route lacks, and omits that the sovereign scraping doc already plans the stage; reword to deterministic-first, persistence-boundary redaction.

title: Procedure store and run-as-procedure, with postconditions so real runs can compile
summary: Persist compiled browser procedures (versioned, tagged, org and owner scoped), add an execute endpoint that replays a procedure through the normal step path with grant, approval and budget checks, and offer 'save as procedure' after a successful agent run. First add optional postcondition assertions to agent steps so typical click, type and select runs can reach Verified status, because the compiler today rejects anything unverified.
whyItMatters: Turning a one-off agent browsing session into a repeatable, schedulable procedure is the step from 'the agent browses' to 'the product automates', and a replay is cheaper than re-planning every run. Quarry already has the hard part (compile, replay-compare, quality and impact checks) which Firecrawl's open source does not expose.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (agent run exported as skill, workflow and schema)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: GET /v2/agent/:id/skill returns {name, spec, skillMd, workflow, schema, blueprint} derived from a finished run (the generator itself is closed upstream, so only the route shape is known). Re-implement as: distill the verified action trajectory into a parameterized procedure (steps, element refs, input schema) plus a natural-language skill; store with a version; replay executes deterministic steps and hands drift back to the agent. Apify adds immutable builds numbered MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD, tag-to-build mapping and pinning, and records the resolved build on each run.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: SRC: compile_procedure, compare_replay, assess_quality and analyze_impact exist behind four stateless endpoints; the compiled procedure is returned to the caller and never stored, version is fixed at 1, and there is no execute-procedure endpoint. compile_procedure rejects any receipt whose outcome is not Verified (browser_procedure.rs:85), but outcome_for_action marks click, type, press, scroll, select and evaluate as Unknown ('postcondition_required'), so a typical form-driving run cannot compile; only navigate, wait, capture, dialog and download steps verify. Receipts are not appended under ZDR, so ZDR runs cannot be compiled at all. The Verevon UI does not call these endpoints and capability-core's skill sink does not take browser trajectories (not verified).

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane: (1) extend the agent step request with an optional expect assertion (URL pattern, ref present, text present) that Quarry evaluates after the action and uses to upgrade the outcome to Verified. (2) Add a procedures table (quarry-control Postgres or edge Postgres): org_id, owner_id, procedure_id, version, tags, steps, source_receipt_ids, status (draft, promoted, quarantined) and the quality report; versions are immutable, tags move, and each run records the resolved version. (3) POST /v1/agent/procedures/{id}/runs starts a run and feeds the steps through the existing step handler, so grants, sensitive approvals and budgets (R-t2-06-01) apply again; on drift return RepairRequired to the planner. Model Plane: 'save as procedure' after a successful run and register promoted procedures as capabilities in capability-core (R-t2-06-07). Frontend: saved procedures list with replay-check and impact status.
dependencies: Coordinate with any automation or scheduling category
risks: Replaying with logged-in profiles must re-check grants and approvals every run, never replay a stored sensitive approval. ZDR runs cannot be saved. Postconditions that are too weak would let a broken replay look verified; keep the unverified-step refusal in assess_quality. Overlaps an automation category.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-06-04] docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:93-96 (persistent rollout state and fixture-backed quality gates for procedures)

verevon.exactGap: Quarry has stateless compile_procedure, compare_replay, assess_quality and analyze_impact (browser_procedure.rs:61-200) behind four routes (agent_routes.rs:3685-3695); the compiled procedure is returned to the caller, version is hard-coded to 1 (browser_procedure.rs:108), nothing stores it, no execute route exists, and nothing outside Quarry calls these routes. compile_procedure rejects any receipt whose outcome is not Verified (browser_procedure.rs:85-96) while outcome_for_action marks click, type, press, scroll, select and evaluate as Unknown (observation.rs:217-262) and StepBody has no expect or postcondition field (agent_routes.rs:818-824), so a form-driving run cannot compile; ref-based actions also embed snapshot_id, generation and ref_id (contracts.rs:650-654) and compare_replay demands exact action equality, so a stored procedure could not replay in a new session without re-binding refs.
reuse: Quarry browser_procedure.rs compile, compare_replay, assess_quality and analyze_impact and the four existing routes: keep stateless and extend.
Durable non-ZDR step receipts (receipts.append at agent_routes.rs:2346-2391, list_for_actor) as the compile source.

Model Plane run-level postcondition: PlanConfig.postcondition and judge_browser_procedure (browser_agent.rs:262-285, postcondition.rs:996-1075) as the run-level verifier to pair with a new step-level expect evaluated by Quarry.
The normal step path /v1/agent/runs/:id/step with BrowserBroker grants, execution-core approval gate (browser_events.rs:238) and max_cost_usd budgets for any replay.
Existing SemanticLocator and ElementFingerprint (contracts.rs) as the stable locators to store instead of run-specific refs.
capability-core and session-core agent_skills registration path (skillsink/sink.go) and capability-core cron for scheduling replays.
verevon.constraints: Quarry's own code and docs put procedure rollout state and business approval outside Quarry: assess_quality 'supplies evidence for the owning release/Model workflow' (agent_routes.rs:2512-2527, browser_procedure.rs:150-152), Quarry 'does not silently replay or self-heal effectful procedures' (agent_routes.rs:2523-2527) and 'Model Plane remains the planner and policy owner' (agent_routes.rs:2462-2466); persistent rollout state is listed as future work (WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:93-96). A Quarry-owned store with an execute endpoint that replays steps would make Quarry the proposer, which breaks 'Model proposes, Quarry executes'. Every replay must re-run grants, sensitive-action approvals and budgets and must never reuse a stored approval; ZDR runs write no receipts (agent_routes.rs:2360-2391) so they can never be compiled or saved.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Keep Quarry's role as deterministic evidence: add an optional step-level expect assertion (URL pattern, ref present, text present) that Quarry evaluates after the action to upgrade the outcome to Verified, and canonicalise stored actions to stable locators (semantic locator or element fingerprint, stripping snapshot_id, generation and ref_id) so replay can re-bind against a fresh snapshot and fail closed on ambiguity. Put the procedure store (versioned, tagged, org and owner scoped, draft/promoted/quarantined) and the runner in Model Plane (capability-core registry or session-core), where the runner proposes each stored step to Quarry's normal step endpoint, uses Quarry's replay-check for comparison, and applies grants, approvals and budgets; 'save as procedure' and the list UI are Frontend work on top.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L: step-level postconditions in Quarry, locator canonicalisation and replay re-binding, a Model Plane store plus runner with approvals and budgets, and UI. It also depends on the live planner loop, grants and budgets (F-t2-001, F-t2-008, F-t2-010). Could be staged: postconditions (M), canonicalisation (M), store plus runner (L).
verevon.verdictReason: The compile, replay-check, quality and impact functions exist and are wired to routes, so the item must say the stateless half is shipped; the missing half is a store, an execute path and postconditions. The proposed placement (Quarry store plus execute endpoint) conflicts with Quarry's documented design and the Model-proposes rule, and the item misses that ref-based actions are run-specific and cannot replay verbatim.

title: Per-run result sets with a dataset table view and server-side export
summary: Give every crawl, batch and extract run an append-only result set (JSONL in the artifact store, indexed by run) behind GET /v1/runs/{id}/items?format=csv|jsonl|xlsx&fields=&omit=, with a dataset table view in the Ingestions page and a per-org retention policy. ZDR runs stream items and persist nothing. Ingestion into the Data Plane stays an explicit, selective decision.
whyItMatters: Users extracting structured data (prices, listings, procurement notices) need a table they can inspect, filter and export without forcing everything into the Data Plane. Today the Ingestions page shows runs, schedules, monitors, sources, evidence and profiles but no result data.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (dataset, key-value store and request queue per run)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Run creation allocates dataset_id, kv_id and queue_id and injects them into the run. The dataset is append-only (items up to 9 MB) and exports server-side with format=csv|jsonl|xlsx|xml|rss, field projection (fields, omit, clean) and hidden #-prefixed debug fields. The KV store holds content-typed records for blobs and state; named storages persist indefinitely while unnamed ones expire after about 7 days; per-object rate limits return 429.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: SRC and baseline: artifact storage (memory, filesystem, S3 with content addressing), a durable Postgres URL frontier and Data Plane ingest exist, but there is no per-run result set, no dataset or key-value API, no export formats and no dataset browser; the SPA's Quarry client (quarry-client.ts) is unused code.

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane: at job completion write each result item to a JSONL object in the artifact store under org/run, with an index row in Postgres, and add the items route with the export formats and projection. Retention policy per org (default expiry, longer for named sets); ZDR returns items on the stream only. Frontend: dataset table view in the Ingestions run detail with an 'ingest to Data Plane' action and a download menu. Optional output schema fields arrive with R-t2-06-06.
dependencies: Optionally F-t2-053 for typed field metadata
risks: Must stay a working set with retention, not a second Data Plane (no retrieval or graph). Export of large sets needs streaming. Items can contain sensitive scraped content, so ACLs follow the run owner.

verevon.exactGap: No per-run result set, dataset or key-value API, export formats or dataset browser exist: the edge route table has artifacts list/get, jobs list, run and job events, sources, snapshots and team aggregates only (routes.rs:130-293), ArtifactSummary has no run_id and the list has no run filter even though artifact keys are laid out org=/run/page_hash/kind/id (resources.rs:83-97, artifact_store.rs:186-200). The Ingestions page has runs, schedules, monitoring, sources, evidence (job events) and profiles but no result data (VerevonIngestionsPage.tsx:67-114); manual extract results are returned once inline as ephemeral evidence under a synthetic run id (ingestions/runs.rs:268-340), and the SPA quarry-client.ts is used only by its own test. Structured /v1/extract is synchronous and persists nothing.
reuse: ArtifactStore with per-run key layout (org=/run_id/page_hash/kind/id) and tenant-bound get_with_key: add a run_id field and filter to the artifact list instead of a second store.

page_extracted events (title, excerpt, summary, word_count, lang, driver; routes.rs:776-830, event.rs) already stored in control per job and served by GET /v1/runs/:id/events and /v1/jobs/:id/events: a ready-made per-page row source for crawl and batch.
Gateway /api/ingestions/runs and /api/ingestions/evidence plus the Evidence panel as the place to attach a results table.
Selective ingest to the Data Plane (crawl ingest flag, CrawlPagePicker) for the explicit promote action.
Quarry retention janitor in control (main.go:197-201, inert unless QUARRY_RETENTION_DAYS is set) for retention policy.
verevon.constraints: ZDR: /v1/crawl and /v1/batch are refused for ZDR callers (routes.rs:555-575), so a durable run result set never applies to ZDR; only synchronous scrape and extract can run under ZDR and those must stay stream-only. The result set must remain a working set with retention, not a second Data Plane (no retrieval or graph); Data Plane ingest stays an explicit decision. ACL: artifact reads are tenant (org) bound (resource_routes.rs:125-155), not per actor, so per-owner result visibility would be new work. Stored items can hold sensitive scraped content, so export must be streamed and audited.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not start with a new JSONL store plus Postgres index plus xlsx export. Smaller path: (1) add run_id to ArtifactSummary and a run filter on /v1/artifacts (S); (2) project per-page rows for crawl and batch from page_extracted events plus artifact refs, exposed as GET /v1/runs/{id}/items with csv and jsonl export streamed by the edge or gateway (M); (3) a table view in the Ingestions run detail with an ingest action. A durable structured result set only becomes meaningful once structured extraction runs as a durable job (today /v1/extract is synchronous and unpersisted), so tie the JSONL dataset design to that dependency rather than to existing runs.

verevon.verdictReason: The feature does not exist and the gap description is accurate, but the proposed storage design overbuilds when per-run artifact keys and page_extracted events already exist. title: Saved job definitions: expose presets, then first-party Quarry packs with typed schemas
summary: Phase 1 (M): expose quarry-control's preset catalog through quarry-edge with org and Space scoping, add 'save as preset' on ingestion runs, and make scrape, crawl and batch schedules actually execute. whyItMatters: Saved, typed job definitions give users and the Model Plane a menu of known-good jobs instead of free-form crawls, and Quarry keeps execution authority by validating (pack id, input) against the schema. A JSON input schema with UI hints (editor, prefill, enum titles, isSecret, resource picker) renders the form and validates API input identically. Tasks are saved input plus run-option presets (up to 5,000 per user) that can be run, scheduled and shared; schedules reference presets. title: Crawl planning: validate/preview endpoint, Model Plane crawl-plan tool and a stronger /v1/map

title: Scrape request context and egress tiers: locale/geo/mobile emulation, country egress with policy-gated auto-escalation, profile pinning and cache partitioning
summary: Add profile_id, location {country, languages} and a mobile/device preset to ScrapeRequest and to lease creation. When a profile is set, the planner must use only profile-capable browser drivers, never the static/TLS tiers, never read or write the scrape cache, and stamp the profile scope into receipts. Apply Emulation.setLocaleOverride, setTimezoneOverride, setGeolocationOverride, setDeviceMetricsOverride and setUserAgentOverride at context creation, tag proxy-pool entries with a country, and include (country, languages, mobile) in the cache key. || Extend ProxyPool and EgressBroker with a vendor-neutral tier (direct/first-party, basic datacenter, enhanced residential or mobile) and an optional country, exposed as proxy: auto|basic|enhanced and country on scrape and agent runs. The broker plans basic first and escalates to enhanced only on rate-limit, transport or region-block outcomes when org policy allows it. The Model never picks the proxy. In a second phase turn the in-memory (host, proxy) health into a SessionPool that scores identities (proxy, cookie jar, fingerprint) and retires bad ones.
whyItMatters: The UI is Norwegian-first, so localized pricing and content matter. Scraping behind a login is only safe for knowledge ingestion if personalised pages can never leak across tenants through a shared cache and if the content inherits the owner's ACL. || Higher success on geo-restricted and rate-limited public sites for both user browsing and agent research, and localized results for market-research use cases, without a per-request choice by the Model. Verevon currently has only a flat proxy list, no geo control in the gateway or UI, and no identity health beyond a 60 s cooldown.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Planner: if request.profile is set, candidate engines are the browser engines that support profiles (parsers only with bytes the browser downloaded). Cache layer: personalised = headers || actions || profile means no cache lookup and no cache store. location validates an ISO alpha-2 country (special pools gated by team permission), chooses egress by country, sets Accept-Language from languages[], timezone from country default, optional coordinates, and mobile sets device metrics plus UA; cache key includes (country, languages, mobile). || Merged items add: Request field proxy: basic|enhanced|auto (default auto). Attempt 1 uses the basic pool. On a block signal (401/403/429 or a challenge hint) a typed 'needs stronger egress' error is caught by the waterfall, which retries once on the enhanced pool inside the same retry budget, with the timeout raised for stronger tiers. Pool choice is encoded as (group, country, sticky session id). Policy can pin the maximum tier per org (Safe Mode forces basic). A SessionPool holds N sessions (proxy session id, cookie jar, score): markGood decays the score, markBad raises it, a blocked status retires the session, and state persists across restarts.

title: Register governed remote browser backends (Kernel, Browserless, Browserbase) behind an egress-containment proof
summary: Expose the backend list and each backend's capability set through the session API, register the already-implemented Kernel and Browserless drivers behind config, and implement the containment proof that lets a remote driver run governed agent sessions (route provider traffic through Quarry's pinned egress proxy or require a provider-side egress allowlist attestation). Today Browserbase is scrape-only and Quarry rightly refuses backends that cannot prove isolated_egress.
whyItMatters: The local lease pool is a hard-coded 2 and one Chromium process, so burst capacity and reliability for the in-app browser and AI runs need a scale-out path that does not change Model Plane tools. Capability flags keep the governance story intact.

title: Isolate each browser session or tenant in its own container or VM instead of a shared Chromium
summary: Lease a container or microVM per browser session (per-org warm pools first, per-session later) with its own Chromium, a tmpfs profile directory, cgroup limits and egress only through the egress broker, destroyed at session end with persistent profiles exported encrypted. Either reuse Model Plane sandbox-manager leasing primitives or build a dedicated browser-pool service owned by the Ingestion Plane; the already present Browserbase, Browserless and Kernel drivers are an alternative route to provider-hosted isolation.
whyItMatters: Tenant isolation for a browser that both users and agents drive on arbitrary sites: a renderer exploit or cross-context leak in a shared Chromium crosses tenants. It is also needed before persistent profiles and downloads are offered more widely.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (isolated per-run containers; SOC 2 Type II; runtime technology not disclosed, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this category (Apify, DOC only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A sandbox manager leases a container or microVM per browser session or tenant: own Chromium, tmpfs profile, cgroup limits, egress through the egress broker only; destroy at session end and export persistent profiles encrypted to storage.

Start with per-org pools and a warm pool to hide cold-start latency; per-session microVMs later.

title: Budgeted web research job contract with run-context cost attribution
summary: Package the existing search, scrape and browser-agent steps as one research run in the Model Plane: input {prompt, urls?, output schema?, max cost/credits, effort}, output {status, data, partial, partialSchemaValid, stopReason such as credit_limit_reached, creditsUsed}, with one active run per thread (409 thread_busy plus the running run id). Quarry accepts a signed run-context header {requestId, parentRunId} from the Model Plane so its cost events attach to the parent run and are not billed twice.
whyItMatters: A predictable, budgeted research call gives other features, and any future external API user, one contract with partial results and a clear stop reason instead of stitching step-level agent routes together. Budgets must be enforced server-side in the Model Plane, since Quarry usage reaches billing-core asynchronously. Crawl starts remain approval-gated (Model proposes, Quarry executes).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not build a new research-run type from raw steps: promote the existing deep_research pipeline to an addressable run (GET status, partial results, stopReason mapped from halt_code, one active run per thread returning 409 and the running run id), map the caller budget onto the existing caps plus a credit or USD ceiling, and add output-schema validation only after the JSON-format item lands. Add the signed run-context header as a separate small cross-plane change (web_tools.rs and the model-gateway Quarry client send requestId and parentRunId; Quarry writes them into UsageEvent.metadata). Defer the external-API-user justification until such a consumer exists.
verevon.effortNote: Reworded scope (addressable wrapper over the existing pipeline, budget mapping, thread-busy guard, run-context attribution) is M because the pipeline and its session run already exist. Output-schema validation and fully durable partial state would return it to L.
verevon.verdictReason: The item proposes packaging steps that deep_research already packages for chat. The real gaps are addressability, a caller budget, thread-busy semantics and run-context attribution to Quarry; reword to those.
